page.running_head: Ex. 2. C. I. De Volunt. Signi

main_text.p: placiti, at non continuo objectum omnis voluntatis beneplaciti est à Deo decretum & volitum voluntate signi, sed id tantum quod verbo revelatur, ut justum aut injustum; & hoc sensu voluntas signi & in præceptionem & prohibitionem, & in rem præceptam & prohibitam terminatur & transit.

4. Quæres igitur, quid voluntas signi nobis exprimat? Resp. exprimere. 1. Hanc esse verbi naturam, ut fidem & bona opera instanter urgeat & persuadeat. 2. Revelare legem & euangelium, nempe sapiens & sanctissimum Dei decretum & beneplacitum de præmiandis obedientibus, & plectendis immorigeris, Micha. 6.8. Indicavit tibi o homo quid sit bonum. Rom. 12. 2, 3. Revelat nobis omnium officium esse & obligationem ut obediant. Obad. 13. Non debebas aspexisse in diem fratris tui. 4. Exprimat denique nobis, Deum simpliciter approbare actuque complacentiæ velle obedientiam hominum, sive actu obediunt, sive non. 1. Sam. 15.20, 21, 22. At vero quod ad actualem obedientiam, voluntas signi formaliter ipsam non vult, hoc est, non hac voluntate intenditur, & sic hæc Deum virtualiter & eminenter velle, quæ jubet, observavitResp. ad artic. 1. Bnd. [?]fius. gravis & eruditus Vir Doct. Gulielmus Ame-feript. Re-tic. 1. Bnd. [illegible, ~8 letters]
5. Hinc multis nominibus differunt voluntas signi & beneplaciti. 1. Differunt ipsis actibus. Nam voluntas beneplaciti est Dei decretum & æterna determinatio de re fienda vel non

page.notes: Marginal notes are small and partly unreadable. The left margin notes "Resp. ad artic. 1. Bnd. fius." and "feript. Re-" are doubtful; the second note's second line is illegible. The line "tic. 1. Bnd." is partly guessed. The long s is read as s throughout. The printed "2i6" at the head is read as 216. Some word forms, such as "sanctiffimum" and "fit", were normalised as described in the rules. The page ends mid-sentence ("vel non") and continues on the next page.
